subject: ent
title: Stridor and congenital laryngeal lesions

steps.tx: **Stridor** is harsh high pitched sound from laryngeal or tracheal obstruction (above carina), distinct from stertor (nasopharyngeal snoring rattle) and wheeze (lower airway musical). Inspiratory stridor localises supraglottis or glottis, biphasic to fixed glottic or subglottic lesions, expiratory to intrathoracic trachea. Any child with stridor gets airway first assessment: position of comfort, oxygen, no throat inspection or separation distress in suspected epiglottitis until theatre airway team assembled.
steps.say: Stridor sings from voice box; stertor snores from nose throat; wheeze whistles from chest. Do not poke epiglottitis throats.

steps.tx: **Laryngomalacia** is commonest congenital stridor: floppy supraglottic structures (omega epiglottis, short aryepiglottic folds, prolapsing arytenoids) sucked in on inspiration from first weeks, worse feeding, supine or agitated, better prone, usually self resolving by 18 to 24 months as cartilage stiffens. Severe cases with failure to thrive, apnoea or respiratory distress need supraglottoplasty. Reflux aggravates airway oedema and is co treated.
steps.say: Newborn inspiratory noise better prone is laryngomalacia. Most outgrow floppy voice box by age two.

steps.tx: Acute stridor emergencies separate by story: viral **croup** (laryngotracheitis, 6 months to 6 years, barking seal cough, steeple subglottic narrowing, night onset, steroids and nebulised adrenaline) versus bacterial **epiglottitis** (unimmunised toddler, toxic, drooling, tripod, thumbprint epiglottis, theatre intubation, Hib) versus inhaled foreign body (sudden choking in toddler, unilateral signs, rigid bronchoscopy), bacterial tracheitis (toxic, croup like but adrenaline unresponsive, purulent airway), anaphylaxis and retropharyngeal abscess.
steps.say: Barking night cough is croup. Drooling tripod toxic child is epiglottitis: theatre, tube, no tongue depressor.

steps.tx: Other congenital lesions present in infancy: **subglottic haemangioma** (stridor from about six weeks, cutaneous beard haemangiomas in half, propranolol responsive), laryngeal webs and atresia (aphonia or distress at birth), vocal cord palsy and tracheo oesophageal anomalies with feeding aspiration. Flexible endoscopy in theatre with anaesthesia grades lesions (Cotton Meyer subglottic scale) guiding observation, medical therapy or airway surgery, while tracheostomy remains rescue for severe fixed obstruction.
steps.say: Birth airway lesions range webs to haemangiomas. Scope grades them; propranolol shrinks subglottic haemangioma.
